+## reference · AI search citation analysis 2026 domains ranked
+
+- 5,000+ queries across SaaS, eCommerce, B2B, health, finance, media were run on five AI surfaces (ChatGPT with browsing, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Google Gemini, Claude with web).  
+- AI citation sets are 3–6 domains per query, far narrower than Google’s top‑10 SERP.  
+- **Reddit** and **Wikipedia** dominate all surfaces; they appear in the top citation slots for the majority of queries.  
+- **Surface bias**:  
+  - *ChatGPT*: prefers reference sites (Wikipedia, MDN, Investopedia) and community forums.  
+  - *Perplexity*: over‑indexes academic sources, primary news, technical docs; cites 6+ sources per answer.  
+  - *Google AI Overviews*: mirrors organic SERP; top‑5 Google ranking correlates with citation.  
+  - *Google Gemini*: pulls heavily from Google properties (YouTube, Maps, Shopping, Knowledge Graph).  
+  - *Claude*: favors long‑form authoritative content and official docs.  
+- **Top 20 cross‑surface domains (Tier 1–3)**:  
+  1. wikipedia.org – entity definitions, factual grounding.  
+  2. reddit.com – first‑hand experience, comparison threads.  
+  3. nytimes.com – primary news, explanatory journalism.  
+  4. bloomberg.com – business & market data.  
+  5. stackoverflow.com – technical Q&A, code patterns.  
+  6. github.com – source code, library docs.  
+  7. reuters.com – wire‑service news, corporate filings.  
+  8. moz.com – SEO definitions, original studies.  
+  9. ahrefs.com – search data, primary research.  
+ 10. mayoclinic.org – clinical overviews, symptom reference.  
+ 11. sec.gov – official filings, regulatory data.  
+ 12. theverge.com – tech news, product reviews.  
+ 13. g2.com – SaaS reviews & comparisons.  
+ 14. hbr.org – management research, B2B frameworks.  
+ 15. developer.mozilla.org – web standards, API reference.  
+ 16. statista.com – aggregated statistics, market sizing.  
+ 17. nih.gov – peer‑reviewed medical research.  
+ 18. techcrunch.com – startup news, funding coverage.  
+ 19. investopedia.com – finance definitions, concept explainers.  
+ 20. youtube.com – transcripts, tutorials (Gemini‑heavy).  
+- **Vertical winners**:  
+  - *SaaS*: G2, Reddit, vendor docs, Stack Overflow.  
+  - *eCommerce*: Reddit, Wirecutter, manufacturer sites, YouTube.  
+  - *B2B Services*: HBR, McKinsey, Gartner, Clutch.  
+  - *Health*: Mayo Clinic, NIH/PubMed, CDC.gov, Cleveland Clinic.  
+  - *Finance*: Bloomberg, Reuters, SEC.gov, Investopedia.  
+  - *Media*: NYT, The Verge, Reuters, Wikipedia.  
+- **Content‑format patterns that earn citations**:  
+  - Lead with a number, clear definition, or named framework.  
+  - Dense comparison tables with consistent columns.  
+  - Reddit posts with “I tried”, “after 6 months”, “difference was”.  
+  - Original research with stated methodology and sample size.  
+- **Citation velocity**: time from publication to first AI citation; high velocity (days) predicts 60–90 days ahead of SEO gains. Track a panel of 50 seed queries monthly across all surfaces.  
+- **Tactical actions for agencies**:  
+  1. Audit presence on all five surfaces, not just Google.  
+  2. Build a clean, well‑sourced Wikipedia entry for the brand/product.  
+  3. Actively participate in 5–10 relevant subreddits.  
+  4. Publish quarterly primary‑data studies with clear methodology.  
+  5. Restructure flagship pages: first 200 words self‑contained, include a quotable fact or comparison table.  
+- **Content investments that grow fastest**:  
+  1. Primary‑data studies (quarterly, downloadable tables).  
+  2. Comparison matrices (vendor/tool/category, updated quarterly).  
+  3. Definition & framework hubs (50–150 short concept pages, each with one quotable fact).  
+
 Sources: https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/ai-search-citation-analysis-q2-2026-domains-ranked
